title: A Hierarchical Tokenization Framework for Voxel-Level fMRI Representation Learning
claim: Encode fine-grained signals once, aggregate them into coarser tokens, quantize and decode at every scale under a shared multi-scale loss.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right pipeline over bottom row of per-scale result plots
description: The top panel is a left-to-right pipeline diagram. A brain icon on the left fans out to three dashed boxes of example BOLD time series: Functional Networks (17), Parcels (DiFuMo-1024) and Raw Voxels (Grouped). These feed a tall blue Raw Voxel Encoder. Its output splits into three horizontal branches, one per scale (voxel, parcel, network). Voxel→Parcel and Parcel→Net aggregation boxes in purple connect the branches. Each branch runs through a blue transformer block, a purple BSQ block and a green quantized-code bar (q_voxel, q_parcel, q_net), then a green decoder. Each decoder outputs a brain surface rendering, from gray (voxel) through speckled (parcel) to bright color patches (network). Dotted lines run from the renders to an L2 loss circle, with the multi-scale loss formula above it. Below a dotted divider, three plot panels compare predicted (blue) and ground-truth (green dotted) BOLD signals at the voxel, parcel and network levels.
caption: Hierarchical tokenization and reconstruction for resting-state fMRI. Voxel-level BOLD signals are organized into a three-level hierarchy spanning sub-parcel voxel groups, parcels (DiFuMo-1024), and large functional networks (Yeo-17). A shared encoder produces voxel-level representations, which are progressively aggregated to parcel- and network-level tokens via hierarchical mappings. At each scale, tokens are discretized using binary spherical quantization (BSQ) and decoded to reconstruct the corresponding signals. The model is trained using a multi-scale reconstruction objective, encouraging representations to preserve information across voxel, parcel, and network levels. Example reconstructions (bottom) illustrate recovery of BOLD dynamics at all scales.
abstract: We introduce HBAR (Hierarchical Brain Activity Representation), a hierarchical tokenization framework for learning compact, multi-scale representations of neuroimaging data. HBAR organizes voxel-level resting-state fMRI into a hierarchy spanning sub-parcel voxel groups, parcels, and large-scale functional networks, enabling up to 415x compression while preserving fine-grained spatial information beyond conventional parcellation. The framework supports fixed atlas-based, fully learned, and softly prior-guided hierarchies, allowing us to systematically study the role of structured priors in brain representation learning. On HCP-YA, at approximately 415x compression, HBAR achieves higher parcel and network correlations than rate-matched flat tokenizers, while at a lower 52x compression rate, shuffling the anatomical grouping reduces parcel correlation from 0.920 to 0.886. Demographic readouts with autoregressive training also reveal potential gains from the hierarchical structure. By combining sub-parcel inputs, compact discrete tokens, and multiscale brain structure, HBAR offers a practical framework for representation learning in high-dimensional neuroimaging data.
